questions.prompt: A cafe gets 100 qualified enquiries and 20 completed paid orders. What is the enquiry conversion rate?

options.a: The number of social media post impressions
options.b: 20 percent: paid orders divided by qualified enquiries
options.c: One hundred percent because every enquiry was observed

questions.feedback: A conversion rate uses verified outcome events divided by a clearly defined eligible population.

questions.prompt: A signup page records 250 eligible visits and 25 completed registrations. What metric is justified?

options.a: 10 percent: completed registrations divided by eligible visits
options.b: Ten percent of this year's unspecified revenue
options.c: Total page visits as a count of completed registrations

questions.feedback: A conversion rate uses verified outcome events divided by a clearly defined eligible population.

questions.prompt: Two transactions have identical prices but different order identifiers. How should a reviewer treat them?

options.a: Retain the records as separate until source records prove duplication
options.b: Delete one because the amounts are equal
options.c: Merge both rows into a new invented purchase

questions.feedback: Cleaning decisions need source validation rather than cosmetic consistency.

questions.prompt: A scheduling dataset contains the date February 31. What should an analyst do?

options.b: Delete every date in the same month
options.c: Flag the invalid date and verify the correct record from the source

questions.feedback: Cleaning decisions need source validation rather than cosmetic consistency.

questions.prompt: A nonprofit compares registrations in three neighbourhoods. Which visual is clearest?

options.a: Unlabelled 3D pie sectors with no exact values
options.b: A chart without any unit or timeframe
options.c: A labelled category bar chart with a zero baseline

questions.feedback: Explicit units and fair scales keep quantitative comparisons interpretable.

questions.prompt: A shop displays weekly PKR revenue by product group as vertical bars. What must be included?

options.a: Decorative widths that change independently of the amounts
options.b: A clearly identified PKR axis, category labels, dates and a zero baseline
options.c: A truncated baseline to make the best category appear much larger

questions.feedback: Explicit units and fair scales keep quantitative comparisons interpretable.

questions.prompt: Purchases rise after two overlapping promotions. What conclusion is defensible?

options.b: State the observed rise and note other possible influences instead of asserting one cause
options.c: Attribute all purchases to the first promotion without comparison

questions.feedback: Analysis must distinguish observations from causal claims and explain limited samples.

questions.prompt: A survey of eight customers from one shop is used to inform a citywide decision. How should it be reported?

options.a: Describe the result as exploratory with sample size and representativeness limitations
options.b: Claim that eight customers represent the entire city reliably
options.c: Discard negative feedback to create a stronger result

questions.feedback: Analysis must distinguish observations from causal claims and explain limited samples.
